name: Alang–Madan–Kulang (AMK)
tagline: Widely called the toughest trek in Maharashtra — technical, exposed, multi-day
seoTitle: Alang-Madan-Kulang (AMK) Trek Guide — The Solo Trail
seoDescription: Honest guide to the AMK range trek near Nashik — Maharashtra's most technical fort trek. Why this is not a solo beginner trek, and what real preparation looks like.

seasons.label: Oct – Mar
seasons.sub: Cool, dry — the only season this trek should be attempted

seasons.label: Jun – Sep
seasons.sub: Monsoon — explicitly not recommended, too dangerous on exposed/technical sections

seasons.label: Apr – May
seasons.sub: Hot, water scarce on the range

seasonNote: AMK is a clear exception to the general Sahyadri rule that monsoon is best — the exposed ledge traverses and rappel at Alang peak become genuinely dangerous when wet.

routeOptions.name: Full AMK range traverse
routeOptions.notes: Technical terrain including exposed ledge traverses and a rappel section at Alang peak. Mountaineering/rope-handling experience and proper gear are expected, not optional. We do not recommend attempting this solo regardless of experience level — go with an experienced, equipped group.

safety.intro: AMK is consistently described by experienced Sahyadri trekkers as the hardest trek in the state. This is not a trek to attempt without technical rope/rappelling experience and a properly equipped group.

alerts.title: Technical terrain — rope and rappelling skills required
alerts.body: Exposed ledge traverses and a rappel at Alang peak mean this trek carries real fall risk for anyone without mountaineering-level experience. Do not attempt without proper gear (harness, rope, helmet) and an experienced group leader.

alerts.title: Do not attempt solo
alerts.body: Unlike most treks on this list, we're not just flagging solo-specific precautions — we recommend against attempting AMK solo at any experience level. Join an established trekking group with technical experience.

cards.title: Before you go
items: Confirm technical rope-handling experience honestly before committing
Book with an established group that provides safety gear and an experienced leader
Plan for 2–3 days — this is not a single-day outing

cards.title: On the trail
items: Follow your group leader's pacing on exposed sections without exception
Test all rope/harness gear before committing weight to it
Carry more water than a standard day trek — no reliable sources on the range

cards.title: Signs to turn back
items: Any rain or fog forecast during your window
Uncertainty about gear condition or fit
Fatigue on Day 1 that would compromise Day 2's technical sections

items.name: Climbing harness + helmet (via your trekking group operator)
Sturdy trekking boots with ankle support
Lightweight tent/sleeping bag for the overnight(s)

gettingThere.intro: This is a 2–3 day technical expedition, not a day trek. Logistics must be arranged in advance through Ambewadi village.

steps.title: Reach Kasara
steps.body: Train from Mumbai or Nashik to Kasara station on the Central Railway — well connected. From Pune, travel via Igatpuri/Ghoti first.

steps.title: Kasara to Ambewadi or Kulangwadi
steps.body: There is essentially no scheduled bus service to these remote base villages — a shared or private jeep must be hired from Kasara, taking 2–3 hrs depending on road and monsoon conditions.

steps.title: Arrange guide and logistics in advance
steps.body: AMK involves rock-climbing sections that require fixed ropes and an experienced local guide. Guide, porter and homestay arrangements are made through contacts at Ambewadi village — book ahead by phone rather than showing up unannounced.

steps.title: Plan the ascent timing
steps.body: Start from the base by 7am to summit Alang before noon and reach the Madan campsite before dark.

gettingThere.permitNote: We strongly recommend against attempting AMK solo without a professional local guide and proper gear. It is widely regarded as the toughest and most dangerous trek in the Sahyadris, with several fatal incidents on record. Treat this as a guided, multi-day, technical-gear expedition — not a solo day trip.

transport.note: Full vehicle; ₹200–400 per person if shared

onTrail.note: Not optional on this trek given the technical difficulty
Via guide — there are no formal rental shops here
Per meal or night across a multi-day trek
